question: how much of the previous distributional branch's 0.8057 UNKNOWN rate is attributable to the four dimensions this audit classifies POSSIBLE OFFSET?
classification: POST-HOC QUANTITATIVE CHECK, run after the verdict was assigned; it changes no model, no threshold and no frozen artifact.
method: re-derive a per-gesture Gaussian/Mahalanobis class model from the FROZEN DB9 representative postures (70/30 split not used; the model is fit on all six-gesture representative postures as a magnitude check) and apply it to the frozen 86 858 paired emg2pose GT frames, once with all 16 dimensions and once excluding the four POSSIBLE OFFSET dimensions.  This is NOT a re-run of the previous branch's fitted models, which used a subject-grouped shrinkage covariance; it is a magnitude check with a plain sample covariance.
reading: excluding the four dimensions lowers the UNKNOWN rate by about 7.5 percentage points, so the broken channels are a REAL but PARTIAL contributor.  Most of the over-rejection survives their removal, which supports Session 5's independent conclusion that a genuine cross-dataset distribution shift exists.  It also shows the previous branch's 0.8057 was NOT purely an artifact of the broken channels - a claim this audit deliberately does not make.
what_this_does_not_say: it does not validate 0.8861 as a corrected figure.  The plain sample covariance over-rejects relative to the frozen pipeline (0.9609 vs 0.8057 on the same 16 dimensions), so only the DIFFERENCE between the two columns is interpretable, not either level.
